lesson_scope: Tangents and normals to circles at a known point on the circumference: radius-tangent perpendicularity condition m_tan = -1/m_rad, normal passing through the centre, tangent equations in ax + by = c and y = mx + c forms, intersection of tangents from symmetric points, and geometric areas of right triangles and tangent kites.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating radius gradient and applying perpendicularity condition for tangent gradient.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of radius and tangent gradients.

hints: Calculate the radius gradient using $m_{\text{rad}} = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$ from $(2, 1)$ to $(5, 5)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the gradient of the radius $CP$ connecting centre $C(2, 1)$ to $P(5, 5)$:
$$m_{\text{rad}} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{5 - 2} = \dfrac{4}{3}$$

The tangent at $P$ is perpendicular to the radius $CP$:
$$m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{1}{m_{\text{rad}}} = -\dfrac{3}{4}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: writing standard tangent equation at a point on circle.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of finding circle tangent equation.

walkthrough.text:
Extract centre $C(1, 2)$ and compute radius and tangent gradients:
$$m_{\text{rad}} = \dfrac{6 - 2}{4 - 1} = \dfrac{4}{3} \implies m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{3}{4}$$

Form the equation of the tangent at $P(4, 6)$:
$$y - 6 = -\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 4)$$
$$4(y - 6) = -3(x - 4) \implies 4y - 24 = -3x + 12 \implies 3x + 4y = 36$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds radius gradient $\dfrac{6 - 2}{4 - 1} = \dfrac{4}{3}$ and perpendicular tangent gradient $m_\perp = -\dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: writing equation of normal to a circle.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of finding circle normal equation.

hints: The normal to a circle at any point passes through the centre $(-1, 3)$.

walkthrough.text:
The normal to the circle at $Q(2, 7)$ is the line connecting centre $(-1, 3)$ and $Q$:
$$m_{\text{norm}} = \dfrac{7 - 3}{2 - (-1)} = \dfrac{4}{3}$$

Write the normal equation in slope-intercept form:
$$y - 3 = \dfrac{4}{3}(x + 1) \implies y = \dfrac{4}{3}x + \dfrac{4}{3} + 3 = \dfrac{4}{3}x + \dfrac{13}{3}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: recognizing horizontal and vertical tangents to a circle.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of horizontal and vertical tangents.

hints: The centre of the circle is $(3, -1)$ and radius is $4$.
At $P(3, 3)$, the radius is vertical ($x = 3$), so the tangent is horizontal: $y = 3$.
At $Q(7, -1)$, the radius is horizontal ($y = -1$), so the tangent is vertical: $x = 7$.

walkthrough.text:
At $P(3, 3)$, the radius connects $(3, -1)$ to $(3, 3)$ along the vertical line $x = 3$. The tangent is horizontal:
$$\text{Tangent at } P: \quad y = 3$$

At $Q(7, -1)$, the radius connects $(3, -1)$ to $(7, -1)$ along the horizontal line $y = -1$. The tangent is vertical:
$$\text{Tangent at } Q: \quad x = 7$$

hints: Complete square on $x^2 + y^2 - 6x - 4y + 5 = 0$: $(x - 3)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 8$, so centre is $(3, 2)$.

walkthrough.text:
Complete the square to find centre $(3, 2)$:
$$(x - 3)^2 - 9 + (y - 2)^2 - 4 + 5 = 0 \implies (x - 3)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 8$$

Find the tangent gradient and line equation:
$$m_{\text{rad}} = \dfrac{6 - 2}{5 - 3} = 2 \implies m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$y - 6 = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 5) \implies x + 2y = 17$$

ai_rubric.observable: Completes square to find centre $(3, 2)$ and evaluates tangent gradient $m_\perp = -\dfrac{1}{2}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of calculating tangent segment length via Pythagoras.

hints: Radius $CP$ is perpendicular to tangent $PT$, creating right-angled triangle $\triangle CPT$ at $P$.

walkthrough.text:
In right-angled triangle $\triangle CPT$ with right angle at $P$, the hypotenuse is $CT = 10$ and $CP = 5$:
$$CT^2 = CP^2 + PT^2$$
$$10^2 = 5^2 + PT^2 \implies PT^2 = 100 - 25 = 75$$

Calculate the exact tangent length $PT$:
$$PT = \sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding tangent equation.

hints: The centre is $(3, -2)$ and point of contact is $P(7, 1)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate radius gradient from centre $(3, -2)$ to $P(7, 1)$:
$$m_{\text{rad}} = \dfrac{1 - (-2)}{7 - 3} = \dfrac{3}{4} \implies m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{4}{3}$$

Write the tangent equation:
$$y - 1 = -\dfrac{4}{3}(x - 7)$$
$$3(y - 1) = -4(x - 7) \implies 3y - 3 = -4x + 28 \implies 4x + 3y = 31$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates radius gradient $m_{\text{rad}} = \dfrac{1 - (-2)}{7 - 3} = \dfrac{3}{4}$, so tangent gradient is $-\dfrac{4}{3}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding area of triangle formed by tangent and axes.

walkthrough.text:
Find the intercepts of the tangent line $4x + 3y = 31$ with the axes:
$$\text{When } y = 0: \quad 4x = 31 \implies x = \dfrac{31}{4} \implies A\left(\dfrac{31}{4}, 0\right)$$
$$\text{When } x = 0: \quad 3y = 31 \implies y = \dfrac{31}{3} \implies B\left(0, \dfrac{31}{3}\right)$$

Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle $OAB$:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times OA \times OB = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{31}{4} \times \dfrac{31}{3} = \dfrac{961}{24}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: identifying symmetric point on circle, determining two tangent lines, and finding their point of intersection.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding symmetric point and tangent equations.

hints: Since $PQ$ is horizontal and $P(1, 5)$ lies on circle centered at $(4, 1)$, $Q$ has $y = 5$. By symmetry across $x = 4$, $Q = (4 + 3, 5) = (7, 5)$.

walkthrough.text:
By horizontal symmetry across the vertical line through centre $(4, 1)$:
$$x_Q = 4 + (4 - 1) = 7, \quad y_Q = 5 \implies Q(7, 5)$$

Calculate tangent equations at $P(1, 5)$ and $Q(7, 5)$:
$$m_{CP} = -\dfrac{4}{3} \implies m_{\text{tan}, P} = \dfrac{3}{4} \implies y - 5 = \dfrac{3}{4}(x - 1) \implies 3x - 4y = -17$$
$$m_{CQ} = \dfrac{4}{3} \implies m_{\text{tan}, Q} = -\dfrac{3}{4} \implies y - 5 = -\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 7) \implies 3x + 4y = 41$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies $Q(7, 5)$ by symmetry across the vertical line $x = 4$ through the centre.
Finds tangent at $P(1, 5)$ as $3x - 4y = -17$ and tangent at $Q(7, 5)$ as $3x + 4y = 41$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding intersection of tangents.

hints: Add the two tangent equations: $(3x - 4y) + (3x + 4y) = -17 + 41 \implies 6x = 24 \implies x = 4$.

walkthrough.text:
Solve the two tangent equations simultaneously:
$$3x - 4y = -17$$
$$3x + 4y = 41$$
Adding the equations: $$6x = 24 \implies x = 4$$

Substitute $x = 4$ into the second equation to find $y$:
$$3(4) + 4y = 41 \implies 12 + 4y = 41 \implies 4y = 29 \implies y = \dfrac{29}{4} = 7.25$$
$$T = \left(4, \dfrac{29}{4}\right)$$

Radius gradient from $C(3, -1)$ to $P(7, 2)$ is $m_{\text{rad}} = \dfrac{2 - (-1)}{7 - 3} = \dfrac{3}{4} \implies m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{4}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the tangent gradient and line equation at $P(7, 2)$:
$$m_{\text{rad}} = \dfrac{2 - (-1)}{7 - 3} = \dfrac{3}{4} \implies m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{4}{3}$$
$$y - 2 = -\dfrac{4}{3}(x - 7) \implies 4x + 3y = 34$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds centre $C(3, -1)$ and calculates radius gradient $m_{\text{rad}} = \dfrac{2 - (-1)}{7 - 3} = \dfrac{3}{4}$, so tangent gradient is $-\dfrac{4}{3}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding triangle area with tangent.

hints: Triangle $CPT$ is right-angled at $P$, with base $CP = r = 5$.

walkthrough.text:
Find point $T$ by substituting $x = 1$ into the tangent equation:
$$4(1) + 3y = 34 \implies 3y = 30 \implies y = 10 \implies T(1, 10)$$

Calculate the lengths of the two perpendicular legs $CP$ and $PT$:
$$CP = r = 5$$
$$PT = \sqrt{(7 - 1)^2 + (2 - 10)^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + (-8)^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10$$

Since $\angle CPT = 90^\circ$, calculate the area of triangle $CPT$:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times CP \times PT = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 10 = 25$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: finding intercepts of general circle, equations of tangents at both intercepts, their point of intersection T, and the total area of the kite CATB.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding x-intercepts and tangent equations.

hints: Set $y = 0$ in circle equation: $x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0 \implies (x - 6)(x + 2) = 0 \implies A(-2, 0), B(6, 0)$.
Complete square to find centre $C(2, -3)$ and $r = 5$.
Radius gradient at $A(-2, 0)$ is $\dfrac{0 - (-3)}{-2 - 2} = -\dfrac{3}{4} \implies m_{\text{tan}, A} = \dfrac{4}{3} \implies 4x - 3y = -8$.
Radius gradient at $B(6, 0)$ is $\dfrac{0 - (-3)}{6 - 2} = \dfrac{3}{4} \implies m_{\text{tan}, B} = -\dfrac{4}{3} \implies 4x + 3y = 24$.

walkthrough.text:
Find where the circle crosses the $x$-axis by setting $y = 0$:
$$x^2 + 0^2 - 4x + 6(0) - 12 = 0$$
$$x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0 \implies (x - 6)(x + 2) = 0$$
$$A(-2, 0) \quad \text{and} \quad B(6, 0)$$

Complete the square to find centre $C(2, -3)$:
$$(x - 2)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 12 + 4 + 9 = 25 \implies C(2, -3)$$

Find the equations of the tangents at $A$ and $B$:
$$m_{CA} = \dfrac{0 - (-3)}{-2 - 2} = -\dfrac{3}{4} \implies m_{\text{tan}, A} = \dfrac{4}{3} \implies y - 0 = \dfrac{4}{3}(x + 2) \implies 4x - 3y = -8$$
$$m_{CB} = \dfrac{0 - (-3)}{6 - 2} = \dfrac{3}{4} \implies m_{\text{tan}, B} = -\dfrac{4}{3} \implies y - 0 = -\dfrac{4}{3}(x - 6) \implies 4x + 3y = 24$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $y = 0$ in circle equation: $x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0 \implies A(-2, 0)$ and $B(6, 0)$.
Finds centre $C(2, -3)$, radius $r = 5$, and forms tangent at $A$: $4x - 3y = -8$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding intersection of tangents and kite area.

hints: Add the two tangent equations: $8x = 16 \implies x = 2$.
The kite $CATB$ consists of two congruent right-angled triangles $\triangle CAT$ and $\triangle CBT$. Total Area $= 2 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times \dfrac{20}{3}\right) = \dfrac{100}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Solve the two tangent equations simultaneously to find $T$:
$$4x - 3y = -8$$
$$4x + 3y = 24$$
Adding the equations: $$8x = 16 \implies x = 2$$
$$4(2) + 3y = 24 \implies 3y = 16 \implies y = \dfrac{16}{3} \implies T\left(2, \dfrac{16}{3}\right)$$

Calculate the length of the tangent segment $AT$:
$$AT = \sqrt{(-2 - 2)^2 + \left(0 - \dfrac{16}{3}\right)^2} = \sqrt{(-4)^2 + \dfrac{256}{9}} = \sqrt{16 + \dfrac{256}{9}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{400}{9}} = \dfrac{20}{3}$$

The quadrilateral $CATB$ is a kite composed of two congruent right triangles $\triangle CAT$ and $\triangle CBT$:
$$\text{Area} = 2 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times CA \times AT\right) = CA \times AT = 5 \times \dfrac{20}{3} = \dfrac{100}{3}$$
